children: Spotify Technology SA (SPOT, Financials) kicks off third-quarter results for the audio streaming firm as Wall Street watches to see if subscriber growth will balance more investment on artificial intelligence and other platform features.
Jefferies analyst James Heaney maintained a Buy rating and increased his price target to $620 from $600, saying Spotify is highly defensible against AI-related disruption.
Consensus is predicting earnings of $3.18 per share and revenue of around 5 billion.
Management guidance is for 788 million monthly active users, including 305 million Premium customers, operating income of 670 million and a gross margin of 32.9%.
Spotify's operational expenses grew 3% on year in the second quarter to 941 million as the business spent on marketing and AI capabilities.
It's also working on an AI remixing capability with Warner Music Group.
Meanwhile, Spotify has been cleaning up the downside of generative AI, eliminating more than 50 million spam music from recommendation feeds this year.
Thursday's earnings will be the next catalyst, and the question is whether margins can rise without sacrificing product investment.

title: Spotify's AI Push Faces a Margin Test
